description: What a brokerage tool can be about, what it can do, and what follows from both. The catalog implements this table; the linter checks that it still does. Edit this file to change the shape of the catalog, and the descriptors will be told they no longer conform.

AccountId.description: A brokerage account. Prefixed and opaque: nothing downstream may read a branch code or an open date out of it.

InstrumentSymbol.description: A listed ticker, uppercase, optionally with a share-class suffix after a dot. The suffix is why a pattern of ^[A-Z]{1,5}$ is wrong: it silently rejects BRK.B.

OrderId.description: One order, for its whole life. A replacement keeps the identifier it was given, so a customer who was read an order number can still ask about it.

ExecutionId.description: One fill. An order may have several; each settles on its own date.

LotId.description: One tax lot: a block of shares bought on one day at one price. Selling is a choice between lots, and the choice is worth money.

ConfirmationToken.description: Single-use authority to place one exact order, issued by a preview and spent by a place. The reason preview-before-place is structural in this catalog rather than merely requested: there is no other source of this value.

Account.label: Account
Account.description: A brokerage account held by a customer. Its type decides more rules than its balance does: a cash account cannot borrow, a retirement account cannot sell short, and a restricted account cannot trade at all.

relations.name: hasBalances
relations.description: The money view of the account.

Instrument.label: Instrument
Instrument.description: Something that can be traded. Named things are ambiguous — three listed companies have Apple in their name, and Alphabet has two share classes — which is why resolving a name to a symbol is a tool rather than a guess.

Quote.label: Quote
Quote.description: The current market in one instrument. Perishable by nature: a quote carries the instant it was taken because a stale quote presented as current is the most expensive kind of wrong answer a tool can give.

PriceHistory.label: Price history
PriceHistory.description: Daily bars for one instrument. Bounded on purpose: a model asked for five years of daily closes will ask for them, read the first thirty and bill the firm for the rest.

Balance.label: Balances
Balance.description: The money in an account, in the four senses a customer means by the question: ledger cash, settled cash, buying power, and total equity. Answering with one number is how an agent tells a customer they can afford something they cannot.

Position.label: Position
Position.description: What an account holds in one instrument, aggregated across its lots, with the weight it carries in the portfolio.

relations.name: madeOf
relations.description: The lots the position is built from.

TaxLot.label: Tax lot
TaxLot.description: A block of shares acquired on one date at one price, with its holding period and its wash-sale exposure. The reason an agent can ask a genuinely useful question before a sale instead of silently selling the oldest shares.

Order.label: Order
Order.description: An instruction to trade, and the only entity in this ontology that an agent can change. Everything expensive about this catalog is downstream of that sentence.

relations.name: filledBy
relations.description: The fills that make up the order.

Execution.label: Execution
Execution.description: One fill: a quantity, a price, a venue and a settlement date. Separate from the order because an order's average price answers a different question from what each fill actually cost.

list.gloss: Return the members of a collection the principal may see, newest or most relevant first, bounded and paged.
list.semantics: No arguments beyond the scope and the filters. Never requires an identifier the agent does not already hold, which is what makes a list tool a safe first move.

get.gloss: Return one named entity, or say plainly that it is not there.
get.semantics: Takes the entity's identifier. Returns NOT_FOUND rather than an empty object, so the agent is never left reading zeroes as facts.

search.gloss: Resolve free text to candidate entities, and refuse to choose between them.
search.semantics: Takes a query the customer said out loud. Returns enough on each candidate for the agent to ask a sensible question. A search tool that silently picks the top hit is how the wrong company gets bought.

preview.gloss: Compute exactly what a change would do, change nothing, and issue the authority to go ahead.
preview.semantics: Tier 1 rather than 0 because it reaches the risk and margin engines and because it mints a ConfirmationToken. Safe to call repeatedly while the customer adjusts the order.

place.gloss: Commit a change the customer has seen and approved.
place.semantics: Requires a ConfirmationToken bound to this exact instruction. Idempotent because the token is single-use: a retry returns the original order rather than a second one.

replace.gloss: Amend a working instruction in place, keeping its identifier.
replace.semantics: Tier 3 like place, because raising a limit by a dollar and buying at that dollar are the same economic act.

cancel.gloss: Request that a working instruction stop, and report what actually happened to it.
cancel.semantics: Tier 2 rather than 3: cancelling reduces exposure rather than creating it. Returns the order's real state, because an order can fill in the moment between the decision and the venue hearing about it.

capabilities.note: The entry point. Nothing else in the catalog can be called correctly until the agent holds an AccountId, and this is the only tool that needs nothing to run.
The other entry point, for the half of the conversation that starts with a company name rather than an account.
Plural because a model comparing three stocks will otherwise call it three times, and three round trips to say one thing is three times the latency and three times the audit.
Produces symbols, which is why 'sell my Apple' can be answered without a search: the holding is already named.
The only producer of a ConfirmationToken, and therefore the only way into the three tools that change anything. Also accepts an OrderId, for previewing a replacement.
No ConfirmationToken. Cancelling reduces exposure, and requiring a priced preview to stop an order would mean a customer in a hurry cannot stop one.

evidenceByRiskTier.0: Conformance lint and handler contract tests.
evidenceByRiskTier.1: Adds a selection evaluation: the agent must choose this tool for the utterances it is for, and not for the ones it is not.
evidenceByRiskTier.2: Adds a trajectory evaluation and a recorded human approval for every invocation.
evidenceByRiskTier.3: Adds dual sign-off on the descriptor, a named kill switch, a refusal suite, and a quarterly re-certification against the live catalog.

dualControlAbove: A notional value above 250,000 USD in a single order.
Any order in an account flagged for review.
Any tool whose dataClassification is restricted.
